title: This Shark Kills With Its Tail at 30 mph and Never Has to Bite

scenes.text: This shark kills with its tail, and it never has to bite.
The thresher's upper tail fin is as long as the rest of its body.
It charges a bait ball, brakes, and whips its tail over its head at thirty miles an hour.
The slap is so violent that gas bubbles out of the water.
One strike stuns several sardines at once. The shark then picks them off, about three or four per hunt.
Filmed in the Philippines in 2013: one slap in three lands. The shark never has to bite.

description:
A shark that kills with its tail and never has to bite.
The thresher shark's upper tail fin is as long as the rest of its body. It rushes a bait ball, brakes, and whips the tail over its head at an average of about 30 mph, so hard that gas bubbles out of the water. One slap stuns several sardines; the shark then eats three or four per hunt. Researchers filmed 25 tail-slaps off Pescador Island in the Philippines and published the study in PLOS ONE in 2013; about one slap in three succeeded.
Which shark has the strangest hunting style?
subject: thresher shark
first_comment: Humpback whales use bubbles to trap fish; the thresher makes bubbles by accident, just from the violence of the slap. Which hunting technique in the ocean impresses you most?
